items.review_rationale: Read local ring of fiber of ring map R→S at q via localized S_q modulo extended contracted prime pS_q and equivalent localization of tensor fiber over residue field.

references.context: Inverse image prime ideal in R under the specified homomorphism.
Prime-localized S ring modulo ideal generated by image of p.
Base-change of S along residue-field map R→κ(p).

references.disposition: Local fiber ring is not the original S_q: quotient by pS_q is essential.

items.review_rationale: Read bare graph of a mapping as subset of X×Y with exactly one output per input, stressing graph-only data do not intrinsically retain codomain type.

references.phrase: unique output y for each x
references.context: For every x∈X exists exactly one y∈Y such that ordered pair (x,y)∈G.

references.phrase: bare graph does not determine codomain Y
references.disposition: Same graph may be embedded in multiple ambient codomains, even with fixed domain.

items.review_rationale: Read mapping f:X→Y as total single-valued assignment from every domain input x to exactly one output y∈Y, retaining typed codomain.

references.phrase: totality for all x in X
references.context: Every domain element has an associated output value.
For each fixed x there is exactly one y∈Y associated by mapping.

references.phrase: function need not be injective or surjective
references.disposition: Single-valued total assignment allows repeated outputs and unused codomain elements.

items.review_rationale: Read typed function as triple (X,Y,G) with graph subset X×Y and total unique output property, explicitly retaining both domain and codomain.

references.context: For each x∈X there exists a unique y∈Y with (x,y)∈G.

references.phrase: domain and codomain are part of mapping data
references.disposition: Unlike bare graph convention, different codomains can distinguish typed maps with identical graphs.
